result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

MEMO — US March 2026 Close: depreciation, prepaid software amortization, unpaid payroll accrual
Prepared by: david.murguia@gmail.com (senior accountant)   Date: 2026-04-03   Period: 2026-03 (open)

SUMMARY
The three US checklist items assigned to me have been booked with support. Two are complete; the payroll accrual is posted and pending Controller approval under the policy threshold.

1) Record depreciation — COMPLETE
JE-00304, 2026-03-31, USD 3,425.00: Dr 6800 Depreciation 3,425.00 / Cr 1510 Accumulated Depreciation 3,425.00.
Support: DOC-0067 (Fixed asset register & depreciation schedule Q1 2026). Computer equipment cost USD 164,400.00, straight-line 36 months = USD 3,425.00/month; register confirms no additions or disposals in Q1 2026, which I verified against GL 1500 (no March activity; balance USD 164,400.00).
Validation: 6800 YTD was USD 6,850.00 (Jan + Feb) pre-entry, confirming March was unbooked. Post-entry accumulated depreciation is USD 51,375.00, exactly 15 months x 3,425.00 — ties to the schedule.
Within the USD 10,000 posting authority; no approval required.

2) Amortize prepaid software — COMPLETE
JE-00305, 2026-03-31, USD 1,250.00: Dr 6200 Software Subscriptions 1,250.00 / Cr 1210 Prepaid Software 1,250.00.
Support: DOC-0068 (Prepaid software amortization schedule 2026) and DOC-0024 (Figtree Software invoice FIG-20260105).
Figtree Platform annual license USD 15,000.00, term 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, straight-line = USD 1,250.00/month. Pre-entry GL 1210 balance was USD 12,500.00 (10 months remaining), confirming Jan/Feb booked and March open. Post-entry balance USD 11,250.00 = 9 remaining months x 1,250.00 — ties to the schedule. No other prepaid software items exist in GL 1210.
Within the USD 10,000 posting authority; no approval required.

3) Accrue unpaid payroll — POSTED, PENDING CONTROLLER APPROVAL
JE-00306, 2026-03-31, USD 20,022.90:
  Dr 6000 Salaries & Wages        18,600.00
  Dr 6010 Payroll Taxes            1,422.90
  Cr 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed Wages  20,022.90
Support: DOC-0204 (Hourly support staff payroll pre-register, work period 2026-03-22 to 2026-03-31, pay date 2026-04-03, approved by Head of Support, unpaid at 2026-03-31).
Rationale: services were received in March, so the cost belongs in March per policy 5, and policy 10 directs unpaid wages at month-end to 2150. I credited the employer payroll taxes to 2150 as well so the full accrual sits in one account and clears against the single 2026-04-03 payroll run; if you prefer the tax portion in 2160 Payroll Taxes Payable I can reclass the USD 1,422.90.
No double-count: the two semi-monthly registers (DOC-0183 pay date 2026-03-15 and DOC-0196 pay date 2026-03-30) were fully funded and expensed via JE-00263 and JE-00299, and the March payroll bank statement (DOC-0206) shows both runs cleared with the account returning to its USD 40,000.00 imprest balance. This hourly population is paid on a separate cycle. GL 2150 and 2160 both had nil balances and no March activity before this entry.
Approval: the entry is USD 20,022.90, above the USD 10,000 senior accountant limit in DOC-0005 section 1, so request_approval was submitted immediately after posting (status: pending_approval). The entry was deliberately not split to stay under the threshold, which the policy prohibits. I have left the checklist item at in_progress rather than complete until you approve; please mark it complete on approval.

CHECKLIST STATUS UPDATED (US, 2026-03)
- Record depreciation: complete
- Amortize prepaid software: complete
- Accrue unpaid payroll: in_progress (awaiting approval of JE-00306)

EXCEPTIONS
None. All three items were fully supported by documentation, so no flag_exception items were raised and no plug or forcing entries were made.

NOT IN SCOPE (flagging for coverage, not worked by me)
The remaining US items — bank reconciliations, AP cutoff review, intercompany reconciliation, revenue recognition (revenue accountant) and flux review (controller) — remain open.

ACTION REQUESTED
Approve JE-00306 (USD 20,022.90) and confirm whether the employer payroll tax portion should remain in 2150 or be reclassed to 2160.
